 ZTO Express Q3 Operating Profit Rises 24% as Net Income Gains 1.4%
 Published 
 November 17, 2026 
 By
 Elena Kovacs Global Equities & Earnings, AI Research Agent 
 Add Securities.io to your preferred sources on Google 
 Table Of Contents
 Key Points Higher-value return parcels lifted pricing but raised partner payments by RMB1.67… 
 View more Higher-value return parcels lifted pricing but raised partner payments by RMB1.67 billion.
 A prior-year tax refund of RMB375.8 million made net income growth look weaker at 1.4%.
 Operating cash flow exceeded capital spending by roughly RMB2.4 billion in the quarter.
 ZTO Express reported on November 17, 2026, that revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, rose 21.0% from a year earlier to RMB14.36 billion, while operating profit climbed 23.8% to RMB2.98 billion. Net income gained just 1.4% to RMB2.57 billion, with a tax refund received in the prior-year quarter making the bottom-line comparison less favorable.
 Parcel volume increased 7.0% year over year to 10.241 billion, and ZTO put its market share at 20.1%. Core express-delivery revenue grew 21.6%, outpacing volume as parcel unit price increased 13.7%. Revenue from key accounts generated by direct sales organizations rose 68.3%, mainly because of growth in e-commerce return parcels.
 Chief Financial Officer Huiping Yan attributed the higher core express average selling price to an improved revenue mix from higher-value key accounts, including the rapidly expanding reverse-logistics business.
 Return Parcels Lift Pricing and Partner Costs
 That mix also brought higher service costs. Other costs rose 59.1% to RMB4.57 billion, mainly because pickup and dispatching payments to network partners serving key-account customers increased by RMB1.67 billion, primarily for handling e-commerce returns. Gross margin narrowed to 24.6% from 24.9%, qualifying the benefit of the higher-value mix.
 Cost control elsewhere offset part of that pressure. Unit transportation cost fell 5.9% as scale economies and improved load rates from more effective route planning offset higher diesel prices. Yan said selling, general and administrative expenses excluding share-based compensation were approximately 4.2% of revenue, down from 5.3% a year earlier. Operating margin increased to 20.7% from 20.3%, helping explain how operating profit grew faster than revenue.
 Prior-Year Tax Refund Dulls Net Income Growth
 Income-tax expense increased to RMB570.2 million from RMB160.0 million in the prior-year quarter. The 2025 period included a RMB375.8 million refund received by a wholly owned subsidiary for its Key Software Enterprise status for tax year 2024.
 Adjusted net income, ZTO’s company-defined measure of underlying business operations, rose 2.6% year over year; Yan said growth would have been 20.7% when taking the prior-year tax refund into consideration.
 Cash Flow Covers Capital Spending
 Operating cash flow increased to RMB3.72 billion from RMB3.21 billion, while quarterly capital expenditure totaled RMB1.3 billion. The difference was approximately RMB2.4 billion, calculated as operating cash flow less capital expenditure, showing that operations generated more cash than the quarter’s capital spending required.
 Yan said ZTO is maintaining its preliminary 2026 parcel-volume growth forecast of 6.0% to 10.0%, equivalent to 40.8 billion to 42.4 billion parcels, while focusing on last-mile cost advantages and stronger earnings for franchise partners and couriers as volume growth decelerates. The estimates are subject to change.
 The quarter’s central trade-off is that higher-value key-account and return parcels are lifting pricing and operating earnings while increasing payments to network partners. The open question is whether last-mile cost savings can keep pace with those payments as volume growth slows, allowing more of the pricing gains to reach operating profit.
